expects.rule: Key metrics sit above the fold, and navigation supports both an overview and a drill-down into detail.
Empty states teach the first step: they explain what will appear and offer the action that fills them, instead of showing an empty chart or table.
Charts offer time-range controls so a period can be compared with an earlier one, and stay readable at small widths.
Colour contrast is sufficient and every control can be reached and used from the keyboard.
Lists of records are tables with sortable columns, saved filters or views, and a visible count and state for each row.
Every screen has one primary action, and destructive actions ask for confirmation or offer undo.
A global search or command entry reaches any object in one step, with a keyboard shortcut shown next to it.

traits: A persistent left sidebar of 5 to 8 top-level items on 4 of 8 sites (Sentry, Attio, Linear, Umami); Plausible and Intercom have no sidebar in the first view.
Metric tiles above a chart: 6 numbers on Plausible, 5 on Umami; tables below with percentages or counts.
Dark or near-black interface on 3 of 8 (Plausible, Linear, Grafana's default); the rest use white or light grey (#f8f9fa, #ffffff).
One typeface family per product screen on 6 of 8 (Inter on Attio and Linear, Rubik on Sentry); a mono face for identifiers on Linear.
One accent colour on the main button or active item (purple on Sentry and Plausible).
Record pages split into a main timeline and a properties panel (Linear, Attio).
Four of the eight can be used with no account (Plausible, Umami, Grafana, Lightdash); Sentry asks only for a work email.

avoid: A dashboard of equal-size cards each holding one big number and a small sparkline, with no hierarchy.
Empty tables or charts with no message and no action on a new account.
Rounded oversized controls and wide padding that show six rows where a user needs thirty.
A hamburger or icon-only sidebar with no labels and no tooltips.
Fake placeholder data (Lorem ipsum, John Doe, round numbers) left in screens.
Modal dialogs for every edit, and no keyboard shortcut for common actions.
